Backlinks are still about 65% of the Google ranking algorithm. That hasn't changed. What has changed is the quality-versus-quantity math. A single link from a high-authority site, a .edu, a news organization, a regional press outlet, is worth tens of thousands of the old-school comment-spam links. Q: What are backlinks, and how do you actually get them? A: A backlink is any time another website links to yours. It signals to Google that your site is real, established, and trusted by others. We build them two ways: a higher volume of lower-quality links through blog placements and automated tools (around 50 per month), and a smaller number of high-quality links through guest posts, partnerships with complementary businesses, and press releases on distribution platforms.
